note: Loan parity-store capability registry. Each capabilities_required name on a vector must map, on the vector's seam, to status exercised, and the capability must be in the graded domain, else the vector is refused (default-deny). Eleven capabilities are graded: the four-bucket repayment allocation (loan-repayment-allocation seam), the single-period schedule-interest rounding of the discriminating SEED-L06 loan (loan-schedule-interest seam), the net disbursal amount (loan-disbursement seam), the derived total-outstanding of the SEED-L03 post-repayment summary (loan-summary-outstanding seam), the persisted loan-status ordinal read-back (loan-status seam), the derived per-row outstandingLoanBalance column of the transactions read-back (loan-transaction-balance seam), the derived debit/credit totals AND per-(transaction, account) side of a loan-produced journal-entry batch (loan-journal-entry-batch-balance seam), whether it holds MORE THAN ONE PAIR (loan 10, L17 + L18) or ONE transaction carrying an odd multi-leg posting whose credits land on at least two DISTINCT accounts (loan 12, the five-leg L53 repayment), and the whole-schedule principal amortization read back from the discriminating SEED-L05 schedule (loan-schedule-amortization seam: the per-period principalDue components sum EXACTLY to the disbursed principal and the final outstanding principal balance is EXACTLY zero, in integer minor units with no residue). The SEED-L01 interest waiver arithmetic is captured but NOT in the graded domain: the loan slice has no interest-waiver arithmetic (interest is not a LoanCharge; LoanCharge.Waive covers fee/penalty charges only), so no vector may require it. The waiver's read-back footprint — a posting that does NOT move the outstanding balance — IS graded, under the transaction-balance capability. The delinquency block read back from the committed loan details at business date 2026-09-01 is graded too (loan-delinquent-days seam): the calendar-day difference between each loan's summary.overdueSinceDate and the business date, present (non-zero) on the three captures that carry an overdue date and absent (pinned 0, not an error) on the two that do not, so a 30-day-month approximation is discriminated. The first observed loan write-off is graded too (loan-writeoff-four-bucket seam): WriteOffOutstanding discharges the outstanding of every unpaid instalment into ALL FOUR buckets — principal, interest, fee and penalty — and the four portions sum to the write-off amount; the observed fee (100.00) and penalty (57.00) are non-zero and DISTINCT, so a port that writes off only principal (or principal+interest), drops either charge bucket, or swaps fee/penalty is discriminated. The append-only journal-entry side of the FIRST observed loan-transaction reversal is graded too (loan-transaction-reversal seam): the same loan-11 write-off reversed the 2026-09-02 interest accrual transaction L46 by ADDING one counter-leg per original leg (JE 134/135 on the OPPOSITE sides, same transaction id, same account, same amount, same transaction date 2026-09-02) while JE 84/86 stay byte-identical and unflagged, so a port that duplicates on the same side (the batch still balances), dates the counter-legs at the write-off business date 2026-09-03, or borrows the DIFFERENT manual reversal path's fresh transaction id or reversed=true originals is discriminated; the write-off's own five-leg L54 posting is a separate observation and is not graded here. The obligationsMet skip is NOT graded: loan 11 has no fully-paid instalment, so skipping none and forgetting the skip sum identically and no drive is registered.

capabilities.name: journal-entry-batch-balance
capabilities.description: TWO properties of a loan-produced journal-entry batch read back from the journal-entries endpoint. First, the derived debit and credit totals, summed independently over EVERY leg: sum(debits) == sum(credits), exactly, in integer minor units. A batch holding MORE THAN ONE PAIR (a disbursement pair plus a fee pair) discriminates a port that sums only the first pair, drops a pair, or nets the two legs on one GL account; a single-pair batch cannot. A single transaction id carrying one debit and credits to at least two DISTINCT accounts (the five-leg repayment L53) is the SECOND discriminating shape: the leg count is ODD, so logic that walks legs two at a time drops the fifth (the single debit), and collapsing the four bucket credits onto one account still BALANCES and still totals correctly, so only the per-(transaction, account) side list sees it. A batch of one debit and one credit is still refused. Second, WHICH account takes WHICH side in WHICH transaction — the per-(transaction, account) side list, keyed on the observed account, not on the account's normal balance. A port that reverses both legs of a balanced pair keeps the two totals equal and still "balances" while crediting the account that was debited; only the side list sees it. The list is graded on the ACCOUNT term too: the fee pair posts to a DIFFERENT account pair than the disbursement (principal moves through OHLGR-Loan-Portfolio/OHLGR-Fund-Source, the fee through OHLGR-Income-From-Fees/OHLGR-Fund-Source), so a port that routes every posting through the disbursement's account mapping keeps all four sides and both totals at the observed values and moves only WHICH GL account a fee leg names — a fee posted to the loan portfolio instead of to income, and every total still balances. The property is per-(transaction, account), not per-account globally: OHLGR-Fund-Source is CREDIT in L17 and DEBIT in L18.
capabilities.evidence: Capture gl-accounting-surface/out/journalentries-all-raw.json under tenant gerege: loan entityId 10 read back four entries — transaction L17 debit OHLGR-Loan-Portfolio 100000.00 / credit OHLGR-Fund-Source 100000.00, and transaction L18 credit OHLGR-Income-From-Fees 100.00 / debit OHLGR-Fund-Source 100.00 — so sum(debits) 100100.00 == sum(credits) 100100.00, and the four (transactionId, glAccountName, entryType.value) triples are the observed side list. The fee pair does NOT reuse the disbursement's accounts: routing L18 through L17's mapping (DEBIT OHLGR-Loan-Portfolio / CREDIT OHLGR-Fund-Source) keeps both totals and all four sides at the observed values and moves only which account a fee leg names. The single-pair loan entityId 12 batch (L20, 100000.00 each way) balances under almost any defect and is not used to grade this property. Capture loan12-four-bucket-allocation/out/journalentries-loan-12-after-raw.json under tenant gerege: loan entityId 12 transactionId L53 read back FIVE legs, one credit per allocation bucket to a DISTINCT account — credit OHLGR-Loan-Portfolio 91203.12, credit OHLGR-Interest-Receivable 6618.53, credit OHLGR-Fees-Receivable 100.00, credit OHLGR-Penalties-Receivable 57.00 — plus the one debit OHLGR-Fund-Source 97978.65 equal to their sum, so sum(debits) 97978.65 == sum(credits) 97978.65. The four credits are exactly the allocation buckets LN-L11 pins (9120312 / 661853 / 10000 / 5700 minor units), tying the allocation seam to this posting seam; the odd leg count and the four DISTINCT credit accounts are what the pair-based and collapse drives move.

capabilities.name: schedule-principal-amortization
capabilities.description: The whole-schedule principal amortization read back from a full repayment schedule: the per-period principalDue components of the repayment periods (period 0 is the disbursement row and carries no principalDue) sum EXACTLY to the disbursed principal, and the final principalLoanBalanceOutstanding is EXACTLY zero, both in integer minor units with no residue. The SEED-L05 loan disburses 4185009 minor units over 12 repayment periods; the components are eleven 348751 plus a final 348748 whose remainder is placed in the LAST period, so a truncating port leaves a 9-minor-unit residue and a port that never places the remainder leaves 348748 outstanding.
capabilities.evidence: Capture loan-5-schedule-raw.json under tenant gerege (single-line JSON, line 1): repaymentSchedule.totalPrincipalDisbursed 41850.09 and repaymentSchedule.periods[0].principalDisbursed 41850.09 transcribe to 4185009 minor units; periods[1..12].principalDue are eleven 348751 and a final 348748, summing to 4185009; periods[12].principalLoanBalanceOutstanding is 0.0. The near-uniform components with a 3-minor-unit residue in the LAST period are what discriminate a truncating or rounding port. The loan-2 schedule (100000.00 disbursed, 10000000 minor units, 12 varying components from 7884.88 to 8796.88, final balance 0.0) carries the same sum-equals-disbursed and final-zero fact and nothing loan 5 does not, so it is not used to grade this capability.

capabilities.name: delinquent-days
capabilities.description: The delinquency block read back from the committed loan details at business date 2026-09-01, tenant gerege: each loan's summary.overdueSinceDate and its delinquent.delinquentDays, the calendar-day difference between the overdue-since date and the business date. loan-2 (summary.overdueSinceDate 2026-08-01) reads 31, loan-1 and loan-5 (2026-07-01) read 62, loan-4 (2026-06-01) reads 92, and loan-3 and loan-L06 (no summary.overdueSinceDate) read 0. On every row delinquent.pastDueDays equals delinquent.delinquentDays. The three non-zero rows span August (31), July (31) and June (30), so a port approximating a month as 30 days reads 30/60/90 and fails every one; the two absent-date rows pin zero rather than an error or a days-since-epoch value.
capabilities.evidence: Committed loan read-backs under .softhouse/capture/loan/out/ at business date 2026-09-01 [.softhouse/capture/seed/out/businessdate-get-raw.json:1 pins BUSINESS_DATE [2026,9,1]], verified before transcription: loan-2-detail-raw.json summary.overdueSinceDate [2026,8,1] / delinquent.pastDueDays 31 / delinquent.delinquentDays 31; loan-1-detail-raw.json [2026,7,1] / 62 / 62; loan-5-detail-raw.json [2026,7,1] / 62 / 62; loan-4-detail-raw.json [2026,6,1] / 92 / 92; loan-3-detail-raw.json (no summary.overdueSinceDate, no delinquent.delinquentDate) / 0 / 0; loan-L06-detail-raw.json (same) / 0 / 0. The arithmetic 2026-08-01->2026-09-01 = 31 (August 31), 2026-07-01->2026-09-01 = 31+31 = 62, 2026-06-01->2026-09-01 = 30+31+31 = 92. The corpus observes pause 0 / grace 0 on every row (delinquencyPausePeriods empty and delinquentDays == pastDueDays), so it does NOT discriminate the paused/grace subtraction, and no observed loan has an overdue date after the business date, so it does NOT discriminate the negative clamp; a capture of a loan with a pause period or a grace setting would be needed to grade those.

capabilities.name: writeoff-journal-entry
capabilities.description: The five-leg journal entry a loan write-off posts in the NOT-charged-off branch of createJournalEntriesForLoanWriteOffs: for each portion (principal, interest, fees, penalties, overpayment) that is > 0, credit that portion's slot GL account, MERGING portions whose slots map to the SAME account at the first slot's position (accountMap is a LinkedHashMap), then debit the SUM once to the losses-written-off slot (or the write-off-reason mapping when one is set). The pinned loan-11 observation L54 has four NON-ZERO portions in four DISTINCT accounts and no overpayment, so a port that posts one debit per portion, debits only the principal (the batch no longer balances), debits the loan portfolio instead of losses-written-off, or swaps the fee and penalty receivable slots is discriminated (the fee 10000 != penalty 5700, so a swap cannot hide). It does NOT grade the same-account merge (product 3 maps the four slots to four different accounts), the zero-portion skip, overpayment, the write-off-reason mapping, or the charged-off branch (loan 11 was not charged off).

capabilities.name: chargeoff-journal-entry
capabilities.description: The merged journal entry a loan CHARGE-OFF posts in the no-charge-off-reason branch of createJournalEntriesForChargeOff: for each portion (principal, interest, fees, penalties) that is > 0, credit that portion's slot GL account, MERGING portions whose slots map to the SAME account at the first insertion position (accountMap and creditsByAccount are LinkedHashMaps), then debit the SUM once per distinct debit account (the principal portion debits CHARGE_OFF_FRAUD_EXPENSE when the loan is marked fraud, else CHARGE_OFF_EXPENSE; interest debits INCOME_FROM_CHARGE_OFF_INTEREST; fees and penalties both debit the income account they map to). Every credit is inserted before every debit, so the result is credits in slot order then debits in slot order. The three pinned observations discriminate a port that ignores the fraud flag (the loan-15 principal debit moves from account 13 to 14), that fails to merge the loan-7 interest+fee+penalty credit (three credits instead of one 14300), and that drops or reorders a leg. The reason-mapped branch is NOT observed, so the port REFUSES a non-empty charge-off-reason mapping rather than guessing it. It does NOT grade the charged-off (pre-existing charge-off reason) loan branch or a zero-portion skip beyond the pinned penalty-only case.

capabilities.name: chargeback-journal-entry
capabilities.description: The journal entry a loan CHARGEBACK posts on a loan that is NOT charged off, the narrow observed branch of createJournalEntriesForChargeback: when the amount is > 0 CREDIT the resolved fund source (the transaction paymentTypeId's payment-channel account when it has one, else the product FUND_SOURCE) with the amount; when the overpayment portion is > 0 DEBIT OVERPAYMENT with it; when principalCredited > principalPaid DEBIT LOAN_PORTFOLIO with the difference, in that posting order. The observed domain has no fee portion, no penalty portion, no paid portion and no charged-off loan, and the port has no field for any of them, so it REFUSES an amount that is not principal + overpayment rather than guessing an unported branch. The three pinned observations discriminate a port that debits the overpayment portion to LOAN_PORTFOLIO instead of OVERPAYMENT (loan-19 moves the debit from account 18 to 10; on loan-21 both debits name account 10, so the first debit's account cell moves), a port that drops the overpayment debit or reorders the two debits (the overpayment debit precedes the principal debit), and a port that credits the wrong account.

capabilities.name: charge-lifecycle
capabilities.description: The money-mutation lifecycle of a single LoanCharge observed on loan 18, tenant gerege: a charge's outstanding is amount minus paid minus waived; a payment increments amountPaid up to the amount and flips the paid flag only when nothing remains; a waiver moves the whole outstanding into amountWaived, clears outstanding and flips the waived flag while leaving paid false. The fee vector (charge 14, OHLGR-Fee-SDD-100, amount 123.45) is created, partly paid 100.00, then fully paid 23.45, so the paid flag stays false through the partial step and flips only when outstanding reaches zero; the penalty vector (charge 13, OHLGR-Penalty-Flat-57, amount 67.89) is created then waived, so the waived flag flips, outstanding clears and paid stays false. Graded through loan.UpdatePaidAmountBy, loan.Waive and loan.UpdateWaivedAmount. It does NOT grade an instalment-fee charge (the LoanInstallmentCharge delegation is out of the port's slice) or the write-off/reversal undo paths.

capabilities.name: loan-status-transition
capabilities.description: The loan lifecycle state machine as observed on tenant gerege: NextStatus(from, event, facts) dispatches an event and DetermineTransition(from, facts) recomputes the status from the balance facts for a loan already active or terminal. The committed captures pin five transitions by their before/after status ids: submit (LOAN_CREATED from INVALID -> SUBMITTED_AND_PENDING_APPROVAL 100), approve (100 --LOAN_APPROVED--> APPROVED 200), disburse (200 --LOAN_DISBURSED--> ACTIVE 300), repaid in full (ACTIVE with repaidInFull && allChargesPaid -> CLOSED_OBLIGATIONS_MET 600) and write-off (ACTIVE --WRITE_OFF_OUTSTANDING--> CLOSED_WRITTEN_OFF 601). Graded through loan.NextStatus (the four event-dispatched transitions) and loan.DetermineTransition (the repaid-in-full balance transition). The facts are the state machine's five balance-derived predicates, never a balance value (I-3). It does NOT grade the overpaid arm, the transfer sub-states, or the LOAN_DISBURSED-from-OVERPAID branch: no committed capture observes an overpaid loan.

seams.name: loan-charge-lifecycle
seams.description: The money-mutation lifecycle of a single LoanCharge observed on loan 18: a charge's outstanding is amount minus paid minus waived; a payment increments paid up to the amount and flips the paid flag only when nothing remains; a waiver moves the whole outstanding into waived and flips the waived flag. The fee vector (charge 14, amount 123.45) is created, partly paid 100.00, then fully paid; the penalty vector (charge 13, amount 67.89) is created and waived. Each step is graded through loan.UpdatePaidAmountBy, loan.Waive and loan.UpdateWaivedAmount.

seams.name: loan-chargeoff-journal-entries
seams.description: The journal entry of the observed loan charge-offs, tenant tierd: for each positive portion the slot account is credited and the corresponding income/expense account debited, portions that map to the SAME account MERGE into one leg at the first insertion position, and every credit is posted before every debit. The loan-7 L19 observation merges its 30.00/103.00/10.00 portions into one 143.00 credit and one 113.00 debit; the loan-15 L44 observation is the same portions with fraud true, moving the principal debit to the fraud expense account 13; the loan-4 L11 observation is penalty-only, debiting INCOME_FROM_CHARGE_OFF_PENALTY. Graded through loan.CreateChargeOffJournalEntryLegs.

seams.name: loan-chargeback-journal-entries
seams.description: The journal entry of the observed loan chargebacks, tenant tierd, on loans NOT charged off: for the positive amount the resolved fund source is CREDIT, then the positive overpayment portion is DEBITed to OVERPAYMENT, then the principal credited beyond paid is DEBITed to LOAN_PORTFOLIO, in that posting order. The loan-14 L69 observation is principal-only (CREDIT account 4 250.00, DEBIT account 10 250.00); the loan-19 L99 observation is overpayment-only (CREDIT 4 250.00, DEBIT 18 250.00); the loan-21 L109 observation is 350.00 = overpayment 250.00 + principal 100.00, with the overpayment debit 241 before the principal debit 242. The chargebacks were posted with paymentTypeId 2, which has no channel mapping, so the product FUND_SOURCE 4 applies. Graded through loan.CreateChargebackJournalEntryLegs.
